original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.

original.description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. original.description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM.

original.description: ObjectivesAssess the feasibility of using physics-based granular dynamics simulation to model the formation of cryovolcanic terrains on Enceladus and derive insights into surface compactness. Develop a proof-of-concept ML model for inferring snow/ice geophysicalproperties (e.g., density, snow water equivalent) by correlating terrestrial in-situ scientific data with satellite remote sensing observations. Initiate the adaptation of classical, optimization-based HDA frameworks to integrate AIderived geophysical safety maps, establishing a baseline for a future hybrid HDA architecture. Conduct an extensive performance and resource consumption benchmark of key AI and HDA software components on representative space-grade hardware, establishing the trade-space between algorithmic capability and on-board computational budgetDescriptionThe ESA Voyage 2050 L4 mission to Enceladus requires an autonomous landing in the South Polar Terrain to achieve its core astrobiological objectives. This environment presents unique challenges that transcend classical HDA capabilities. Landing hazardsare not only geometric (e.g., slopes, rocks), but also geophysical. Due to the unknown load-bearing capacity of cryovolcanic surface deposits, landing sites can appear perfectly flat and clear of hazards and yet be catastrophically unsafe. Classical existing Hazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) frameworks targeting Moon and Mars, are highly mature for geometric hazard assessment but are not designed to infer subsurface geophysical properties from remote sensing data. This activity shall address this critical technology gap by investigating the integration of AI/ML-based geophysicalinference into a proven HDA decision-making architecture. Additionally, the severe power and computational constraints of a solar-powered missionto Saturn imposea hard limit on the complexity of on-board AI. It is currently unknown what level of "intelligence" is achievable within a realistic resource budget. This activity shall perform the foundational trade-off analysis required to inform mission designers of the necessary hardware and power provisions for a reliable and capable AI-augmented HDA system
